findings.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() applies math.floor/ceil directly to an audit-log datetime, causing TypeError and 500 responses when building cursors
OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor() leaves integer cursor values unconverted instead of returning a UTC datetime, causing timestamp-versus-integer database comparisons on follow-up requests
The negative-offset branch slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start index, which Django rejects and allows crafted negative cursors to trigger a 500

goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

adjudication_records.issue_text: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor() leaves integer cursor values unconverted instead of returning a UTC datetime, causing timestamp-versus-integer database comparisons on follow-up requests

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. Looking at the diff, OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor() simply returns `cursor.value` directly without any conversion. This paginator is used for audit logs which are ordered by '-datetime' (a datetime field). The DateTimePaginator (the original paginator) would convert cursor values to datetime objects for proper comparison. However, OptimizedCursorPaginator returns the raw integer value, which would cause type mismatches when building queries that compare against datetime fields. The get_item_key method also uses math.floor/ceil on the value treating it as a number, confirming this paginator doesn't handle datetime conversion properly for the audit log use case.
